podcast.name: Week in Review

turns.text: Hello, and welcome. It's Sunday, November 8th. I'm Natasha, and this is Week in Review from MMH Daily.
Hi everyone, I’m William. We have a busy day.
We begin with health care.
Ministry of Health discusses draft revised Food Safety Law with international representatives and foreign embassies.

The drafting committee for the revised Food Safety Law held a working session with the Delegation of the European Union and the embassies of 12 countries to discuss recommendations concerning the draft legislation on the afternoon of November 6.
There’s also this: From QR codes to digital communities.

QR codes are becoming digital addresses for residents in rural areas of the central province of Quang Tri, helping delivery workers locate homes, rice traders find collection points and emergency services reach patients. The initiative is also laying the groundwork for forming digital communities at the grassroots level.
On the economic front.
Vietnam sets key economic targets for 2027.

General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and State President To Lam, on behalf of the Party Central Committee, signed Conclusion No. 106-KL/TW, dated October 15, 2026, of the fourth meeting of the 14th Party Central Committee on socio-economic development, state budget implementation in 2026 and plans for 2027.
There’s also this: Accelerating public investment disbursement.

By the end of October 2026, many localities had achieved high public investment disbursement rates, thereby boosting economic growth. However, a substantial volume of capital remained to be disbursed in the final two months of the year.
Now to politics.
Top leader calls for a modern, safe, efficient coal industry, upholding spirit of "discipline and unity".

Upholding the tradition of "Discipline and Unity", General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and President To Lam called for building a modern workforce, improving workers’ skills, promoting technological innovation and ensuring better living conditions.
There’s also this: Top leader and spouse depart for official visit to Japan.

General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and President To Lam, his spouse Ngo Phuong Ly and a high-ranking Vietnamese delegation left Hanoi on November 8 for a four-day official visit to Japan at the invitation of the Japanese State.
Finally, society.
Vietnamese culture shines at festival in Australia.

Vietnamese Consul General in Perth Pham Hai Anh called on the Vietnamese community there to preserve the language, family traditions and national values, actively promote Vietnamese culture internationally and encourage creativity to bring national culture closer to the world while harmonising tradition with modernity.
There’s also this: When OCOP products become tourism resources.

No longer confined to shop shelves, One Commune One Product products are increasingly being incorporated into journeys to explore nature, experience local culture, and discover rural life. This approach is helping Ho Chi Minh City make better use of its local resources, expand markets for agricultural products, and create fresh impetus for rural economic development.
In the Vietnamese-language press, 6 more health stories are in today’s paper, covering tenders, policy and hospitals.
And that’s our show. Every story is in today’s paper, with summaries in Vietnamese. I'm William. Talk to you tomorrow.
And I'm Natasha. Goodbye for now.

51838ff89c93.t: Hoàn thiện quy định quản lý chất lượng thuốc cổ truyền, vị thuốc cổ truyền, dược liệu
